newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks ease on finance sector worries.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks ease on finance sector worries.

text.p: Thai stocks drifted down in during early trade on Wednesday as asset quality and liquidity concerns sparked further sales of finance shares, traders said.
The SET Index lost 4.17 points, or 0.85 percent, to 488.96 by 0405 GMT. The SET 50 eased 0.30 points, or 0.86 percent, to 34.62 in low volume trade worth 424 million baht.

"The policies the government announced are going to take time and everybody knows that. The end of the second quarter is coming from which finance firms have to announce non-performing loans and that has people worried," said a senior trader at Dynamic Eastern.
A senior local executive said on Monday non-performing loans in the finance sector may be as high as 31.5 percent of total lending.
A parliament debate on the 1997/1998 budget that started on Wednesday presented few surprises to the market, traders said.
Brokers said the market is more concern about sustained tight liquidity which pushed the overnight interbank rate this week to 17-20 percent with interfinance rates being quoted even higher.
The finance sector had dipped 5.73 percent by 0421 GMT though steady performance of defensive bank and communications counters halted a broader market fall.
Dhana Siam was most actively traded, falling 1.25 baht to 13.50, Bangkok Bank gained one to 115, and Shinawatra Computer and Communications added eight to 143.
